meta.title: Save in Swiss francs and earn the protocol rate | Frankencoin
meta.description: Hold ZCHF, the decentralized Swiss franc stablecoin, in the savings module and earn the protocol rate. Withdraw any time. Live rate, calculator and three steps to start.

hero.title: Swiss francs that|earn {rate} a year.
hero.subtitle: The franc has held its value for fifty years while the dollar melted. Saving in francs used to mean a Swiss bank and almost no interest. ZCHF changes both.

cards.title: Borrowers pay
cards.description: People mint ZCHF against collateral and pay interest upfront into the protocol's reserve.

cards.title: Savers are paid first
cards.description: The savings module pays the governance-set rate out of that income, before anything goes to shareholders.

cards.title: No lock-up
cards.description: Withdraw part or all of your balance whenever you want, interest included.

items.title: Get ZCHF
items.body: Bank transfer from a Swiss or SEPA account via Mt Pelerin (0% fees), or swap from USDC, USDT or ETH.

items.title: Connect a wallet
items.body: Any Ethereum wallet works. Savings run on Ethereum and seven other chains.

items.title: Deposit
items.body: One transaction. Prefer a token you can trade or use as collateral? Use the Savings Vault (svZCHF) instead.

faq.a: No. ZCHF is a token on public blockchains and you hold it in your own wallet. No issuer can freeze it, and nobody insures it the way a Swiss bank deposit is insured.
Yes. Your ZCHF and the interest it earned can be withdrawn from the savings module whenever you want.

faq.q: Do I pay tax on the interest?
faq.a: Probably, depending on where you live. The app's [accounting report](https://app.frankencoin.com/report) lists the interest you collected per year.

faq.q: How is this different from holding USDC?
faq.a: You hold Swiss francs instead of US dollars, and the protocol pays a savings rate. See the [comparison](/compare).

cta.title: Francs that pay you to hold them.
cta.body: Buy ZCHF by bank transfer or swap, deposit once, withdraw whenever you like.

tbills.title: Why not just buy T-bills?|Because the yield is in dollars.
tbills.subtitle: Treasury bills are the classic safe dollar. Here is what {amount} did since {year}: rolled into 3-month T-bills every quarter, against the same money changed into francs and left at Swiss cash rates.

tbill.label: {amount} in T-bills since {year}
tbill.note: Every T-bill coupon reinvested. Still a loser after US inflation.

chf.label: {amount} changed into francs in {year}
chf.note: {chf} then, earning Swiss cash rates, changed back to dollars today.

tbills.need: Needed just to keep up with US inflation: {need}

reasons.title: The yield was real. The dollar was not.
reasons.body: T-bills paid {tbillAvg} a year on average since {year}. The dollar lost {fxLoss} against the franc over the same stretch, and that ate the whole advantage and more.

reasons.title: A 6% dollar is roughly a 3% franc
reasons.body: The forward market prices the expected currency drift into the rate gap, so a high dollar yield and a lower franc yield tend to land in the same place. With ZCHF the {rate} is in francs: no currency to get wrong.

reasons.title: No broker, no US account, no settlement days
reasons.body: T-bills need a brokerage or TreasuryDirect and, for non-Americans, tax paperwork. ZCHF needs a wallet: deposit in one transaction, interest accrues daily, withdraw any time.

reasons.title: Backed by collateral you can inspect
reasons.body: A T-bill is a government's promise. ZCHF is backed by over-collateralized loans visible on-chain, with a reserve that absorbs losses before savers do. Check the live figures on the Transparency page.

tbills.source: Annual averages from FRED: 3-month Treasury bill TB3MS, H.10 exchange rates, BLS CPI-U; Swiss cash rates from the SNB (call money to 1998, SARON from 1999). Returns ignore taxes and fees. Past moves do not predict future ones; ZCHF carries smart-contract and collateral risk.

problems.title: Saving in francs was great. Doing it was not.
problems.subtitle: The franc kept its value, but keeping francs never paid.

items.title: Banks paid nothing, then charged you
items.description: Swiss cash rates sat near zero after 2008 and went negative from 2015 to 2022, when the SNB policy rate was −0.75%. Banks passed it on: large franc deposits cost money to hold.

items.title: Hard to open from abroad
items.description: For non-residents, a Swiss bank account means compliance hurdles, minimum balances and account fees that make small and medium savings impractical.

items.title: A Swiss bank in your pocket
items.description: ZCHF puts francs in a wallet you control, on eight chains, usable in DeFi or spendable by card, and the savings module pays {rate} in francs, set by governance.

problems.attribution: Points from conversations with the Frankencoin Association.
